name: The Library / Hall of Records
hint: Stacks recede past seeing. The script on the spines will not hold still.

elements.because: A reading room is walked, not floated through; a ground plane gives the stacks something to stand on and the traveller a floor to cross.
"tiered galleries" rising around the reader - a lattice gives the storeys their repeating vertical structure without enclosing the hall in a tunnel the way a vault does.
"tiered galleries" - a repeating bay structure down one side reads as stacked reading levels rather than a single storey.
"tiered galleries" - the facing side, so the traveller walks a nave between two galleries as the reports describe wandering among the stacks.
"shelves and stacks" - a long shelf block running with the hall; depth is set from the vault length so the stacks run out past where the eye resolves them.
"stacks receding beyond sight" - the opposing rank, which is what makes the recession legible as repetition rather than as one wall.
"volumes whose covers and pages carry living, self-rearranging script" - a deep relief face closing the far end, so the recession terminates in worked surface instead of empty fog.

The atlas records "ancient language or hieroglyphics repeatedly observed" in the 36-interview field corpus, and this realm's description makes that script "the substance of an entire place" - so the living-script primitive is the room's content, not decoration on it.
"stacks receding beyond sight" needs the recession to end in worked surface rather than fog, so a wide deep-relief face closes the far end of the hall.
